AbstractText.Label: Background
AbstractText.content: Most dengue patients experience mild disease, dengue fever (DF), while few develop life-threatening severe disease, or dengue hemorrhagic fever/dengue shock syndrome (DHF/DSS). No laboratory tests predict DHF/DSS. We evaluated whether serum chymase can predict DHF/DSS in adult and pediatric patients and the influence of pre-existing conditions (PECs) on chymase levels.

AbstractText.Label: Methods
AbstractText.content: Serum chymase levels were measured in patients presenting with undifferentiated fever to hospitals in Colombo District, Sri Lanka. The value of serum chymase concentration and clinical signs/symptoms as predictors of DHF/DSS was evaluated by multivariate analysis. We assessed the influence of age, pre-existing conditions (PECs) and day post fever-onset on the robustness of chymase as a biomarker for DHF/DSS.

AbstractText.Label: Results
AbstractText.content: Elevated chymase in acute phase blood samples was highly indicative of later diagnosis with DHF/DSS for pediatric and adult dengue patients. No recorded PECs prevented chymase elevation during DHF. However, certain PECs (obesity and cardiac or lung-associated diseases) resulted in a concomitant increase in chymase levels among adult DHF patients.

AbstractText.Label: Conclusions
AbstractText.content: These results show that acute dengue patients who present with high levels of serum chymase consistently are at greater risk of DHF. Chymase is a robust prognostic biomarker of severe dengue for adult and pediatric patients.
